answer:
Cache projected keys and values, not queries or hidden states. A new token projects only its own Q/K/V and attends to the appended cache; chunked decoding additionally needs a causal mask offset by the old cache length. Cache state is returned to the caller, keeping simultaneous requests isolated. Concatenation is clear but copies old state each step; production implementations use preallocated or paged buffers. Supply positional encoding with absolute positions and compare incremental output against a full causal pass in evaluation mode.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** At step $t$, $K_{1:t}=[K_{1:t-1};k_t]$ and $a_t=\operatorname{softmax}(q_tK_{1:t}^T/\sqrt{d_h})V_{1:t}$. Caching removes repeated projection and earlier-token computation, but the new query still reads its entire allowed history. Test multi-token cache appends as well as one-token generation because their causal masks differ. [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.06180)

For the implementation or system context discussed above, see [1](https://magazine.sebastianraschka.com/p/coding-the-kv-cache-in-llms) and [2](https://kipp.ly/transformer-inference-arithmetic/).
